text:
Mixbar 

 Every app, exactly as loud as it should be. 
A native macOS menu bar mixer with per-app volume — no audio driver, no account, no telemetry. 

 
 
 
 
 

 
 Download ·
 简体中文 ·
 User guide ·
 使用说明 ·
 Changelog 
 

 

 Why

macOS has one volume for everything on the machine. Turning the music down also turns the meeting down; muting a game mutes the notification you were waiting for.

Mixbar gives each app its own level. It runs on Core Audio Process Tap — no virtual driver, no kernel extension, no hijacking of the default output device. Quit it and your Mac behaves exactly as before.

 Features

- Per-app volume, 0–200%. The slider follows perceived loudness (50% ≈ −12 dB). Anything above 100% passes through a peak limiter instead of clipping.
- Independent mute per app, remembered across launches.
- Per-output-device memory. Headphones and speakers each keep their own balance; switching restores it automatically.
- Presets. Save the current mix as a named scene — "Meeting", "Late night" — and recall it in one click.
- Global hotkeys. ⌥⌘↑ / ⌥⌘↓ step the frontmost app's volume; ⌥⌘M mutes it. No accessibility permission needed.
- Menu bar quick menu. Right-click the icon to set the frontmost app's level, apply a preset, or pause mixing.
- System notification sounds as one row. macOS plays every notification and alert through systemsoundserverd . Mixbar exposes it as a single System sounds slider, so all notifications get quieter together while app audio stays where you put it.
- Choose what you control. "Don't control" moves an app to an ignored list; restore it any time.
- Output device picker , with hardware volume and mute when the device supports it.
- Frosted glass, your call. Turn the glass off for an opaque background, or dial its transparency.
- Self-healing. If a playing app's pipeline stops rendering while its tap still mutes the app, Mixbar rebuilds the pipeline instead of leaving the app silent.

 Requirements

- macOS 14.2 or newer. Built and measured on macOS 26.6.2, Apple Silicon.
- The prebuilt release is arm64 only. Intel Macs can build from source; that path is untested.
- System Audio Recording permission on first use — macOS asks once.

 Install

1. Download Mixbar-1.4.0-macOS-arm64.zip and unzip it.
2. Move Mixbar.app to /Applications .
3. First launch: right-click the app → Open . The build is ad-hoc signed, not notarized.
 If macOS still refuses, allow it in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway .
4. Open the panel, turn on Independent volume , and play something. macOS will ask for
 System Audio Recording ; allow it and press Retry in the panel if a row reports it is not controlled.

 Usage

Click the menu bar icon to open the panel.

 Area What it does 
 --- --- 
 Device name and large percentage System output volume. Click the device name to switch outputs. 
 App rows Drag to set an app's level, click the speaker to mute. Past 100% the row turns amber with a bolt icon. 
 System sounds row One slider for every notification and alert macOS plays, from any app. 
 Slider icon in the card header Save the current mix as a preset, apply one, or delete one. 
 Ignored list Apps you chose not to control. Restore any of them here. 
 Footer switch Pause mixing entirely; every app returns to its own audio path. 

 Hotkeys — ⌥⌘↑ / ⌥⌘↓ / ⌥⌘M act on the app in front. Turn them off from the icon's right-click menu.

 Menu bar — right-click for the frontmost app's level (100/75/50/25/mute), your presets, and the hotkey toggle, without opening the panel.

 Appearance — ⋯ → Appearance… ( ⌘, ) toggles the frosted glass and its transparency.

The full walkthrough is in the user guide (中文版).

 How it works

Each controlled app gets a private CATapDescription(stereoMixdownOfProcesses:) and its own private aggregate device. The tap mutes the app's original output ( mutedWhenTapped ) and the aggregate plays the same audio back with gain applied — nothing is heard twice, and no system output device is changed.

Gain ramps smoothly (25 ms). Boosted audio passes a peak limiter (ceiling ≈ −0.5 dBFS, instant attack, 160 ms release, one gain shared by all channels). Device and process enumeration runs off the main thread, and taps are built in the background, then installed only if the row still wants them.

Mixbar never records audio, writes no audio files, and makes no network requests.

 What it does not do

- No equalizer, effects, or spatial audio.
- No recording or transcription.
- No per-browser-tab volume — browsers expose a single audio client.
- No per-app notification split. Notifications are controlled as one system-wide row. Apps that hand notifications to macOS — WeChat, Mail, Calendar — are covered by that row, but so is every other app's notifications.
- WeChat voice messages, video and calls are ordinary app audio and are controlled per app. Its notification sound is not.

 Build from source

Requires macOS with the Command Line Tools and an SDK that includes Process Tap.

 

There is no Xcode project and no third-party Swift package.

 Compatibility

Built and measured on Apple Silicon, macOS 26.6.2. Deployment target is macOS 14.2. Not yet verified: Intel Macs, macOS 14.x and 15.x, Bluetooth switching, AirPlay, multichannel interfaces, protected audio, long-run stability.

 Privacy

No account, no telemetry, no network access. Audio exists only in memory, in real time. Preferences live in local.mixbar.audio on this Mac.

 Troubleshooting

 Symptom Fix 
 --- --- 
 No apps listed Play audio in an app first; the list follows audio clients. 
 A row says it is not controlled Allow System Audio Recording in System Settings, then press Retry in the panel. 
 Nothing changes at exactly 100% By design: at unity Mixbar leaves the app on its original audio path. Move the slider away from 100%. 
 Sound seems doubled It should not happen — the tap mutes the source. Pause and resume mixing if it does. 
 Gatekeeper blocks the app Right-click → Open, or allow it in Privacy
